zh.title: 阿聯酋航空與大韓航空等業者推動退役客機組件再利用
zh.summary: 阿聯酋航空與大韓航空等業者推動退役客機組件與舊制服再利用
body: 阿聯酋航空工程部門（Emirates Engineering）日前展示一座高達2.4公尺的發光雕塑作品，該作品以退役的空中巴士 A380 與波音 777 客機組件打造而成。這座雕塑融合了 A380 起落架硬體、鈦金屬引氣管道、複合材料地板面板以及波音 777 機身外皮，用以紀念該航空公司與 Arsenal 足球俱樂部合作20週年，並將持續於 Emirates Stadium 展示。

瑞士國際航空（SWISS）則利用旗下退役的空中巴士 A321 客機（國籍標誌暨登記號碼 HB-IOC）推出「SWISS Recraft Collection」系列產品。這架曾服役於 Swissair 與 SWISS 的客機在27年服役期間累計飛行超過73,000小時並載運逾700萬名旅客。在完成拆解零件備用與訓練用途後，剩餘的機身外皮、內部結構與舷窗等材料被設計師重新打造為行李牌、鑰匙圈、壁掛鉤、衣帽架、碗盤、鏡子、邊桌及舷窗壁掛吧檯等物品。
新加坡航空亦透過其升級再利用計畫（Upcycling Project），將退役客機的組件與材料提供給設計師、藝術家、零售品牌及教育機構。相關材料被轉化為包款、家具、服飾、配件與餐具等產品，並與新加坡在地教育機構及支援身心障礙人士的機構 SG Enable 合作，銷售所得收益將回饋給參與製作的創作者。
大韓航空則將關注焦點投向維修人員的舊制服再利用。隨著今年導入環保新制服，該公司與專門從事升級再利用的品牌 Nukak 合作，將700件退役的冬季外套改造成2,000個耐用的工具包，配發給旗下維修團隊使用，進一步落實航空營運中的永續發展理念。

en.title: Airlines Repurpose Retired Aircraft Components and Uniforms into New Products
en.summary: Emirates, SWISS, Singapore Airlines, and Korean Air are repurposing retired aircraft parts and uniforms into new items.
body: Emirates Engineering has constructed a 2.4-meter-high illuminated sculpture representing the Arsenal crest, crafted from components recovered from retired Airbus A380 and Boeing 777 aircraft fleets. The project incorporates A380 landing-gear hardware, a titanium bleed-air duct, composite floor panels, and Boeing 777 fuselage skin. Created to mark 20 years of partnership between the airline and Arsenal, the sculpture will remain on display at Emirates Stadium as part of a broader trend giving retired aircraft materials a second life.

SWISS has introduced the SWISS Recraft Collection, utilizing parts from a retired Airbus A321 registered as HB-IOC. Over its 27-year career with Swissair and SWISS, the aircraft accumulated more than 73,000 flight hours and transported over seven million passengers. Following standard part-out processes for spare parts and training, designers repurposed remaining fuselage skin, substructure, and aircraft windows into items including baggage tags, key fobs, wall hooks, coat racks, bowls, mirrors, side tables, and wall-mounted window display cases.

Singapore Airlines is extending the useful life of decommissioned aircraft components through its Upcycling Project by supplying parts and materials to designers, artists, retail brands, and educational institutions. Aircraft materials have been transformed into products including bags, furniture, clothing, accessories, and service ware, while artists have crafted sculptures. Additionally, SIA partnered with Singapore-based educational organizations to supply components for design courses and collaborated with SG Enable, returning sales proceeds to participating creators.

Korean Air has repurposed decommissioned maintenance personnel uniforms into operational gear to promote sustainability. Following the introduction of eco-friendly uniforms earlier this year, the carrier partnered with upcycling specialist Nukak to convert 700 decommissioned winter jackets into 2,000 durable tool pouches for its maintenance teams.
